sources.title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
sources.authors: Tilmann Gneiting and Adrian E. Raftery
sources.claim: Logarithmic and quadratic/Brier scores are strictly proper categorical scoring rules; zero-one score does not identify the whole distribution; categorical outcomes are mutually exclusive.
sources.passage_locator: Section 3.1, printed pp.362–363 (PDF pp.4–5), Examples 1–4; Section 2.3 printed p.362; Section 2.2 printed p.361
passages: the sample space ... consists of a finite number m of mutually exclusive events
The scoring rules in Examples 1–3 are strictly proper. The score in Example 4 is proper but not strictly proper.
Example 1 (Quadratic or Brier score)
Example 3 (Logarithmic score)
Scores for competing forecast procedures are directly comparable if they refer to exactly the same set of forecast situations.
the optimal Bayesian decision maximizes expected utility
sources.method_data_model_scale: Mathematical characterization/review over general probability spaces, categorical examples and weather case study; no Jeff-like neural-language training benchmark. Categorical formulas and assumptions, not weather effect sizes, used here.
sources.limits: Strict propriety is an expected-score property under the outcome distribution, not finite-sample calibration, verified labels, or a guarantee that a misspecified/optimized neural model finds that distribution. Paper takes scores as rewards; findings use their negatives as losses.
sources.jeff_relevance_gap: Supports retaining probability-oriented CE and evaluating Brier separately from top-1. Does not select a sample-efficient loss for 1,500 correlated language decisions with varying option sets. Hinge scale and choice-set arguments in findings are explicit mathematical deductions, not paper experiments.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
sources.authors: Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger
sources.claim: Temperature scaling is a single positive scalar fitted by validation NLL, preserves predictions, and often improves matched-distribution calibration; calibration, NLL and top-1 can diverge.
sources.passage_locator: Section 2 Eq.1 PDF p.2; Section 3/Fig.3 PDF p.4; Section 4 PDF p.4; Section 4.2/Eq.9 PDF p.6; Section 5 PDF pp.7–8/Table 1
passages: P(Y-hat = Y | P-hat = p) = p
neural networks can overfit to NLL without overfitting to the 0/1 loss
We assume that the training, validation, and test sets are drawn from the same distribution.
uses a single scalar parameter T > 0 for all classes
T is optimized with respect to NLL on the validation set.
temperature scaling does not affect the model’s accuracy
The only dataset that temperature scaling does not calibrate is the Reuters dataset.
Any calibration model with tens of thousands (or more) parameters will overfit to a small validation set
sources.method_data_model_scale: Vision: Birds, Cars, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, SVHN; ResNets, DenseNets, Wide ResNets, LeNet. NLP: 3-layer DANs on 20 News/Reuters and TreeLSTMs on binary/5-class SST. Validation sizes include 872 SST-binary, 1,097 Reuters, 2,259 20 News, 5,000 CIFAR and 25,000 ImageNet. Table model numerals indicate depths, not parameter counts. Compared temperature with binning/isotonic/BBQ/vector/matrix scaling.
sources.limits: Mostly fixed-label classification and same-distribution evaluation; Reuters already low ECE and does not improve with temperature. Paper emphasizes ECE using 15 bins; tiny correlated Jeff data cannot support importing that binning choice or assuming effectiveness. No parameter-count equivalence to Jeff claimed.
sources.jeff_relevance_gap: Cheap one-scalar post-hoc diagnostic is transferable computationally, not a demonstrated repair for rule transfer, wrong ranks, changing alternatives or teacher correctness. Cross-fitting/group weighting/bounded search in findings are proposed engineering controls, not Guo's protocol.

sources.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
sources.authors: Chujie Zheng, Hao Zhou, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Minlie Huang
sources.claim: Decoder MC selection can depend on answer-ID token priors and option ordering; removing answer IDs is not a universally beneficial fix.
sources.passage_locator: Abstract; Section 2.1 Experimental Setup; Sections 2.4–2.5; Section 3.1; Appendix A Fig.6
passages: Through extensive empirical analyses with 20 LLMs on three benchmarks
we access the output probabilities of option ID tokens A/B/C/D/E and use the maximal one as the model prediction
These results confirm that the model’s token bias is one primary intrinsic cause of selection bias.
the model’s position bias is somewhat present but quite irregular, largely depending on models and tasks
removing option IDs usually degrades model performance (except in a few cases under the 5-shot setting)
The next-token prediction probabilities of the option IDs ... is used as the observed prediction distribution.
sources.method_data_model_scale: 20 causal decoder LLMs: LLaMA-7/13/30/65B, Llama-2 and chat-7/13/70B, Vicuna v1.3-7/13/33B and v1.5-7/13B, Falcon/base-instruct-7/40B, GPT-3.5-turbo-0613. MMLU, ARC-Challenge, CommonsenseQA; varying two to five options and zero/few-shot prompting. Open models use option-token probabilities; GPT-3.5 uses first generated token at decoding temperature zero. Proposes permutation-based prior estimation (PriDe).
sources.limits: Token-bias conclusion is empirical in these models/prompts and does not imply all selection bias is token bias. ID-removal ablation changes prompt naturalness and text-likelihood scoring. Does not measure Jeff encoder or Qwen0.5B; no imported effect sizes or recommendation to modify frozen decoder scoring.
sources.jeff_relevance_gap: Motivates interpreting decoder symbol probabilities cautiously and reporting existing order aggregates; pair-scorer permutation invariance/denominator/IIA statements in findings are architectural derivations, not claims from this decoder study.

sources.title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
sources.claim: Selective prediction trades coverage for accepted risk; coherent ranking may suffice for selection, but guaranteed risk needs explicit sampling/threshold-selection controls and adequate data.
sources.passage_locator: Section 2 definitions and Eq.1 PDF p.2; Section 3 Eq.2 and Lemma 3.1/Eq.4 PDF p.3; Algorithm 1/Theorem 3.2 PDF p.4; Section 4 PDF p.5; Sections 5.1–5.3 PDF pp.6–7
passages: sampled i.i.d. from P(X,Y)
the ideal confidence-rate function should only provide coherent ranking rather than absolute probability values
Whenever the triplet S_m, delta and r* is infeasible, the algorithm will return a vacuous solution with zero coverage.
this training and test sets where each of approximately 5000 samples
the sizes of the training and test set were approximately 25,000
For this simple baseline we found that in over 50% of the cases (1000 random train/test splits), the bound r* was violated over the test set
sources.method_data_model_scale: Post-hoc Selection with Guaranteed Risk over a trained classifier; threshold on softmax response or MC-dropout, binomial risk bound and correction across threshold-search steps. CIFAR-10/100 VGG-16, ImageNet VGG-16 and ResNet-50; ~5,000 calibration and ~5,000 assessment examples per CIFAR experiment, ~25,000 each for ImageNet. Reported confidence parameter delta=0.001. No full parameter counts needed/assumed.
sources.limits: IID sample requirement does not hold automatically for Jeff variants/source correlations or adaptive reuse. Guarantees are not transferable from the vision results; the paper's own footnote notes cross-risk-target multiplicity was not Bonferroni-corrected. Better coverage may be impossible at a chosen target. The illustrative zero-error formula in findings is an algebraic specialization of Eq.4, not a measured result.
sources.jeff_relevance_gap: Supports risk-coverage diagnostics and refusing a naive threshold certificate on 12 groups. Does not certify selective correctness on caller-selected options, unseen policies/mechanisms or imperfect teacher labels.

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
sources.authors: Geoffrey Hinton, Oriol Vinyals, Jeff Dean
sources.claim: Actual teacher probability vectors/logits carry information absent from hard labels; temperature-softened distillation is not verbal confidence or a post-hoc calibration guarantee.
sources.passage_locator: Section 1 soft targets; Section 2/Eq.1; Section 2.1/Eqs.2–4; Section 3 MNIST; Sections 4 and 6 speech scale
passages: use the class probabilities produced by the cumbersome model as ‘soft targets’ for training the small model
use a weighted average of two different objective functions
it is important to multiply them by T^2 when using both hard and soft targets
in the high temperature limit, distillation is equivalent to minimizing ... provided the logits are zero-meaned separately for each transfer case
The total number of parameters is about 85M.
about 2000 hours of spoken English data, which yields about 700M training examples
only 3% of the data (about 20M examples)
sources.method_data_model_scale: MNIST: 60,000 cases; large two-hidden-layer network with 1,200 rectified units per layer, smaller 800-unit layers and further size variants. Speech: 8 hidden layers of 2,560 units, 14,000 HMM labels, ~85M parameters, 10-model teacher ensemble and ~700M training frame examples. Uses high-T soft-target CE plus hard-target CE; 3%-data soft-target regularization experiment still ~20M examples. JFT specialist section not used as support for Jeff.
sources.limits: Strong teacher/generalization and informative distributions are prerequisites, not guaranteed properties. MNIST missing-digit bias adjustments were optimized on test performance, so those anecdotes are not a safe Jeff validation protocol and are not used as recommendations. Fixed taxonomy, huge data scale and acoustic/digit inputs differ substantially from free-form grouped choices.
sources.jeff_relevance_gap: Distinguishes hard teacher supervision from distribution distillation; does not justify requesting new labels, inferring distributions from generated confidence text, or claiming sample efficiency/calibration for Jeff. Verbal-confidence distinction is conceptual, not a new empirical verbal-confidence benchmark.

coverage_limits: No raw Evaluation/probe/final artifact inspection, saved-prediction computation or fresh local empirical outcomes.
No empirical verbal-confidence source or conformal-risk survey; no claim of exhaustive literature coverage.
Relevant passages read using existing fetch/PDF extraction tools; no package installs, model loads, inference, training, tests or lint.
All costs and implementation-time projections in findings are explicitly assumptions/estimates, not measurements.
